name: Landingi
tagline: Landing pages, popups, experiments, lead capture, and agency workflows

pricing.notes: Working normalization from the official public pricing structure. Recheck the source page immediately before publication.

tiers.name: Build
tiers.limits: 10 active landing pages; 2,000 visits/month; 1 custom domain; 5 users; 2,500 credits/month

tiers.name: Optimize
tiers.limits: 100 active landing pages; 30,000 visits/month; 3 custom domains; 10 users; 10,000 credits/month

tiers.name: Scale
tiers.limits: Unlimited active pages; 100,000-500,000 visits/month depending configuration; 10 custom domains; unlimited users; 20,000 credits/month
tiers.notes: Starts at the stated price; final price varies with the selected traffic allowance.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Unlimited active pages; 1M+ visits/month; 100 custom domains; unlimited users; 60,000 credits/month
tiers.notes: Starts at the stated price; final enterprise configuration may vary.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; 14-day trial capped at 200 visits, after which the trial ends
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (annual advertised as 2+ months free; current annual promotional equivalents are lower than a simple two-month discount)
pricing.hiddenCosts: Extra domains cost $5/month each (with plan-specific add-on ceilings); credit top-ups cost $15 for 5,000, $25 for 10,000, or $40 for 20,000; Scale pricing increases with selected monthly traffic.

verdictSummary: The visible landing-page platform loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. Landingi earns its keep through editor, CMS, hosting, polish, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build a focused landing-page platform generator that edits structured page sections, previews responsive layouts, and publishes static files.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
whyPeopleStillPay: Landingi: A single site is easy to code. People pay for safe ongoing edits, templates, publishing, domains, collaboration, and no-maintenance hosting.
ongoingBurden: Maintain responsive rendering, browser compatibility, deployment, domains, forms, spam protection, backups, and editor migrations.

alternatives.name: Mautic
alternatives.desc: Pages, forms, campaigns and A/B tests without licence fees; database and email operations replace the subscription.

alternatives.name: systeme.io
alternatives.desc: Hosted pages, popups, forms and one split test on a permanent free plan; agency workflow is thin.

rejectedAlternatives.name: GrapesJS
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A library for building the editor, with none of the campaign product around it.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Webstudio
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A page builder without managed popups, experiments, lead operations or agency workflow.

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of Landingi is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for Landingi, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a focused landing-page platform generator that edits structured page sections, previews responsive layouts, and publishes static files.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: CMS collaboration and client handoff; managed hosting, forms, and analytics; general-purpose visual editing.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
